A ceasefire/Hormuz reopening announcement over the weekend or Monday would spike equity futures, send oil lower, and improve June CPI forward outlook. Watch for: any IRGC statement on tanker clearance, any back-channel ceasefire signal from Qatar.

events.label: July CPI release (est.) — most important inflation data of the summer
events.note: May CPI 4.2% triggered 9 FOMC hike dots and regime breach on June 17. June CPI (released ~July 14) is the next recalibration: if CPI holds ≥ 4.0%, hike probability for July 28-29 FOMC spikes materially; if CPI falls to ≤ 3.7%, the rate path softens and BUY regime can re-open.

events.label: June CPI (8:30 AM ET) — FactSet consensus ~3.8% YoY (range 3.75-3.90%); BUY gate requires ≤3.5%
events.note: June CPI is the summer's regime-defining binary. FactSet consensus: -0.1% MoM / ~3.8% YoY; gasoline -10% in June (ceasefire-era Hormuz reopening) drives headline step-down from 4.2% May. BTC Gate 2 BREACHED ($61,821 24h low < $62,000 floor) pre-print. Scenario A (CPI ≤3.5%): BUY upgrade activated at 9:31 AM; Gate 2 reset condition met; full NVDA/AVGO/SKHY adds; close TBT immediately. Scenario B (3.5-3.9%): STEP ASIDE maintained; muddle-through; Warsh determines next move. Scenario C (≥3.9%): BEARISH escalation; 30Y through 5.15%; reduce all longs. CRITICAL: June CPI captures pre-Hormuz-shock prices. July CPI (August BLS) carries the real pass-through from July 13 WTI +9.4% spike.

events.label: JPM, GS, WFC Q2 bank earnings pre-market; post-CPI regime reset session
events.note: First major bank Q2 prints following June CPI. Banks are positioned to benefit from higher rates (NIM expansion) but face loan-loss risk if the rate environment begins to pressure credit quality. A clean JPM/GS beat with stable credit quality = 'higher for longer is not recessionary' → constructive for AI longs. NIM miss or rising provisions = growth scare signal. Arrives the day after CPI, when the regime framework for July-August will have been reset by the June print.

events.label: PLTR Q2 2026 earnings AH — $1.94B (+93% YoY); US commercial +149%; FY26 raised to $8.15B; AH toward $142
events.note: RESULT: Revenue $1.94B (+93% YoY) vs. $1.81B consensus. US commercial revenue +149% YoY (vs. +98% expected) — the structural shift from a DoD-urgency story to a broad enterprise-AI story. US government revenue beat as well. FY26 guidance raised to $8.15B (+82% YoY) vs. $7.65B prior consensus. Rule of 40 score: 155%. AH range $123.66–$142.91; settled toward $142 (+11.8% from ~$127 day close). CEO Alex Karp: 'This quarter was otherworldly.' Options swing of ~12% materialized precisely. The morning's central uncertainty — whether Iran de-escalation would unwind the DoD urgency premium — was answered empirically: US commercial grew faster than government, confirming AI adoption is enterprise-wide, not defense-urgency-driven. Day session: SPX ~7,602 (+1.5%), Dow 53,178 (all-time record), ISM Manufacturing 55.6% (4-year high). September hike settled at 64.5% (below 70% trigger) despite hot ISM, on sustained oil deflation (WTI $79.62, −6%).

events.label: JOLTS June 2026 (BLS, 10 AM ET) — 7.36M vs 7.40M est; labor cooling continues
events.note: RESULT: June JOLTS job openings 7.36M (vs 7.40M estimate, vs 7.54M revised May prior). Quits rate 2.0%, layoffs rate 1.1% — steady. Healthcare and leisure/hospitality saw largest declines. Below-estimate print pushed September hike probability from 60.5% (morning) to ~54% (Kalshi end-of-day). Combined with WTI collapsing to $76.14, the rate-relief trade extended: 10Y −5bps to 4.64%, 30Y −3bps to 5.20%. The morning's scenario: 'below 7.0M provides incremental support for the oil-deflation rate-relief narrative' — the actual 7.36M was above 7.0M but below the 7.40M estimate, providing moderate support consistent with the neutral-to-bullish labor read.

events.label: AMD Q2 2026 earnings AH — $11.5B (+50% YoY), data center $6.7B (+107%); AH −8%
events.note: RESULT: Revenue $11.536B (+50% YoY) vs $11.31B consensus. Data-center segment $6.7B (+107% YoY), above $6B consensus but below the $7B bull threshold. EPS $1.66 vs $1.55 estimate. Q3 2026 guidance $13.0B ±$300M (~41% YoY). Non-GAAP gross margin 56%. AH reaction: −8% from $518.58 regular-session close (implied ~$477). The morning's sell-the-news warning was accurate: AMD had rallied from $484 (Monday close) to $518 during the day before reporting, compressing the beat margin. A $6.7B data-center result is objectively strong (+107% YoY, above $6B consensus) but below the $7B threshold the elevated $518 entry implied the market needed. Two consecutive AI hardware beats (PLTR Monday, AMD Tuesday) produced opposite AH reactions: PLTR +11% AH, AMD −8% AH — entry price differential was the determining factor.

events.label: SPCX first public earnings AH — $7.81B (+92% YoY) beats; $18.37B capex miss; AH −7%
events.note: RESULT: SpaceX first post-IPO earnings. Revenue $7.81B (+92% YoY) vs $6.93B estimate — beat by 12.7%. AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY). Connectivity (Starlink) $4.29B (+66% YoY). Net loss narrowed to $541M from $1B. EPS −$0.09 vs −$0.26 estimated. Capex $18.37B vs $13.22B estimated — $15.83B attributed to AI infrastructure. AH reaction: −7% (−8% at worst) on capex spike. Starlink profitability was the bull catalyst investors needed; it did not arrive in the Q2 print. The 2.35x capex-to-revenue ratio (spending more than twice revenue on capex) is VC-scale capital deployment in a public market. Stock is −45%+ from June IPO high of $225.64. December 2026 lock-up expiry remains the structural supply overhang.

events.label: ADP Private Payrolls July — +44K actual (softest of 2026; below 75K consensus)
events.note: RESULT: ADP July private payrolls +44,000 — softest monthly gain of 2026, well below consensus of ~75K and June's revised 95K (down from 98K). Goods-producing employment: −3K. Services: +47K (Education & health +36K; Financial +10K). Pay growth: job-stayers +4.4% YoY, job-switchers +7.0% YoY. The ADP miss was the softest read since early 2025 — below even the August 5 morning bull-case floor of 80K. However, September hike odds ROSE from 54% to 58% (Kalshi) because Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari appeared on CNBC the same morning calling for gradual hikes starting September: 'now is the time to start slowly moving rates up.' Kashkari cited tariff goods prices, fertilizer disruptions, and AI infrastructure capex as supply shocks monetary policy must address regardless of labor softness. 30Y fell only 2bps to 5.169% — Kashkari absorbed the ADP rate-relief impulse. ISM Services same morning: 54.1% (missed 54.5% est.); Employment 47.4% (contraction). NFP Friday August 7 is the next test.

events.label: US-Iran Hormuz interim deal — NOT signed August 5; talks extended to by Friday
events.note: RESULT: Deal not signed on August 5 as targeted. CNN analysis August 5 puts 50:50 odds on a deal by Friday August 7. WTI held $75.69 (−0.1%) — market priced progress but not a formal signing. The August 5 morning called for a formal 60-day interim signing 'today or tomorrow' (Bessent quote); that prediction did not materialize. Talks continue via Oman. The deal has failed twice in 2026 previously. A signing opens the next oil leg toward $68-70; a collapse returns WTI above $78 and re-triggers both oil-side regime breaches. See updated calendar entry for August 7 Hormuz window.

events.label: SpaceX exclusive Nvidia Vera Rubin commitment — Musk confirms AI infrastructure exclusively on NVDA
events.note: RESULT: During SpaceX's first public earnings call (August 4 AH, reported August 5 regular session), Musk confirmed SpaceX will build its AI infrastructure 'exclusively' on Nvidia's Vera Rubin architecture. Targets: 2GW compute by end-2026, 10GW by end-2027. $15.83B of the $18.37B Q2 capex attributed to AI — the largest single-company AI hardware commitment publicly disclosed this cycle. Market reaction: NVDA +3.4% to ~$220 (new high); AMD −6.7% to $483.49 (competitive displacement read-through — SpaceX was the highest-capex new AI infrastructure buyer and chose the rival explicitly); AVGO −6.6% to $392.23 (SpaceX chose commodity NVDA over AVGO's custom-silicon model). SpaceX's 10GW target at Vera Rubin specs requires TSM N3/N2 advanced nodes — constructive for TSM utilization (+2.5% to ~$416).

events.label: SPCX lockup first tranche (20%) — 911.5M shares; closed −13.7% at $108.27, below $135 IPO price
events.note: Outcome (Aug 6 close): First-tranche lockup selling confirmed. SPCX closed $108.27 (−13.7% from $125.33 prior close); intraday range $105.11–$115.75 shows institutional buyers below $110 but close is $26.73 below the $135 IPO price and 52% below the June $225 ATH. Pre-market showed $93 overshoot that did not hold. The liquidation template is established: insiders are monetizing the first 20% tranche. Next unlock trigger post-Q3 earnings (~October). Q3 Starlink profitability and AI segment revenue above $2B are the only catalysts that could interrupt the pattern before December.

events.label: Iran Hormuz restrictive draft — Khamenei still unresponsive; oil held at close of session
events.note: Outcome (Aug 7 close): Khamenei did not publicly respond to the restrictive Hormuz draft. President Pezeshkian described communication as 'very difficult at the moment.' Oil held near thresholds: Brent $82.15 (−0.41%), WTI $78.31 (+0.03%) — both below their $85 and $79 triggers. Despite the massive NFP miss (−23K), the Hormuz uncertainty limited the 30Y's relief to 3bps (5.20%→5.17%). The 3% vs 5-7% transit fee gap between Oman and Iran is the remaining sticking point. The deal has failed to close three times in 2026; each miss was followed by an oil recovery from the dip. Resolution carries forward to the weekend/Monday open.

events.label: July NFP (BLS, 8:30 AM ET) — ACTUAL: −23K vs +80K est; September hike collapses to 36%

events.label: Bessent 'Operation Economic Outcast' — 60+ entities targeted; Chinese banks warned but not sanctioned; Brent fell to $93.16, $94 trigger deactivated
events.note: RESULT: Bessent held press conference Aug 24 announcing 'Operation Economic Outcast' — 60+ entities/vessels targeted across Iran's oil shipping, financial, crypto, gold, and aviation ecosystem. Explicitly warned Chinese banks ('no one is above the reach of US sanctions') but did not include them in round one. Beijing absorbs ~534,000 bpd of Iranian crude (down from 823,000 bpd July); flows untouched. Oil read the package as targeted-not-comprehensive: Brent fell 1.4% to $93.16, deactivating the $94 regime trigger that had been active since Friday's $94.39 close. 30Y eased approximately 4bps to ~5.24%, 6bps from the 5.30% trigger. VIX fell from 16.01 Friday to 15.13. Bessent also previewed a 'major financial institution announcement' by week's end — unquantified secondary catalyst if it targets Chinese crude buyers. BTC tagged $80K intraday ($80,012 high) before settling at $78,989.

events.label: US-Canada 50% tariffs effective midnight — $28B of Canadian goods; Carney declares Canada 'at war with the US'
events.note: RESULT: 50% tariffs on $28B of Canadian wine, cement, lumber, and electronics took effect at midnight Aug 23-24 after trade talks collapsed Friday night. PM Carney Aug 24 statement: 'We are at war with the United States'; accused Trump administration of seeking to destroy Canada's core industries — steel, aluminum, and autos — with unfair terms, and said the US 'wants to destroy Canada firms.' Carney confirmed Sept 8 retaliatory tariffs (dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, electronics) remain on schedule, dollar-for-dollar. Canada retaliatory tariffs arrive 8 days before September 16 FOMC. Manufacturing supply-chain stress at 13-month high as of Aug 22 PMI.

events.note: RESULT: Revenue $2.74B (+37% YoY, +13% QoQ), beat consensus ~$2.71B. EPS $0.94 (in-line). Q3 guidance $3.15B midpoint, +4% above $3.03B consensus. events.label: Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (Aug 27–29) — Warsh keynote Aug 28; neutral on rate path
events.note: RESULT: Warsh's keynote (Aug 28, 10 AM ET) titled 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy' — first Jackson Hole theme centered on digital payments and financial technology. Warsh focused on a first-principles monetary framework review (five internal task forces: communications, balance sheet, economic data, productivity and jobs, inflation frameworks) and declined to signal the September rate path. September hike odds held at ~33% unchanged. 30Y closed Aug 28 at 5.199%, 10bps inside the 5.30% trigger; S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed flat to modestly positive. Bessent 'major financial institution' sanction was not announced by end of business August 28 despite 'by week's end' commitment from August 24. Markets interpreted the speech as neutral: not hawkish enough to compress multiples, not dovish enough to formally deactivate the rate-regime trigger.

events.label: Bessent 'major financial institution' sanction — deadline passed without announcement
events.note: RESULT: No announcement made by end of business August 28 despite Bessent's 'by week's end' commitment (from August 24 Operation Economic Outcast press conference). Brent held near $87.65, well inside the $94 trigger. The Chinese-bank sanction scenario — the 15% tail risk for the week — did not materialize. Warsh's 10 AM ET keynote proceeded without the oil-spike overlay. The sanction remains pending; no revised timeline as of August 28 close.
